en: The Apadāna of the Elder Giripunnāgiya Naḷamāli Chapter 7.7 I was a king named Giribrahmadatta, And I possessed a park called Punnāga. There, I planted many trees, Such as mangoes, breadfruit, and jackfruit. I gave them water and manure, And I tended them with great care. When they were fully grown and flourishing, I provided them with protection. I gave them shade and fruit to eat, And I offered them water to drink. Because I gave such gifts there, I attained a state of happiness. Having passed away from that human life, I was reborn in the world of the gods. For eighty-four thousand years, I enjoyed celestial bliss. Then, having fallen from that divine realm, I was reborn among humans once more. In every birth I took thereafter, I always found abundant wealth. I was born into a wealthy family, Possessing great fortune and power. I was handsome, virtuous, and wise, And I lived a life of great prosperity. Through the merit of those past deeds, I have now become a monk. Having seen the Truth, I have attained The state of an Arhat, free from taints. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Giripunnāgiya, The seventh in the Naḷamāli Chapter.
“The Fully Enlightened One named Sobhita was then dwelling on Cittakūṭa;
having taken hold of a mountain-punnāga tree, [he stood] there.”
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [as before] ... the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Giripunnāgiya Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Giripunnāgiya is the seventh.
